quotes.text:
Scary, right?  

Even scarier -- the bill House Republicans passed contains a provision that bans states from ANY regulations on AI for the next 10 years.  The Senate needs to stop this. https://t.co/hjbaRidQC0

the majority attempted to condition BEAD funding on States agreeing to not regulate artificial intelligence for 10 years. I am concerned about how this would threaten online safety, jeopardize data privacy, and spread misinformation.

The growth of AI, both in use and in development, has spurred an explosion in data-center construction, which has caused a huge rise in demand for the electricity they need to function as well as for water used by some data centers' liquid cooling systems.

First, data centers are causing residential customers' electric bills to rise by increasing electricity demand and straining the electric grid. [...] It is possible to build more data centers in a way that doesn't hamper innovation but also benefits the communities that surround them. We should be thoughtful and purposeful about the way we are building data centers.
Emerging technologies like AI and blockchains are redefining how people around the world live and work.

AI tools of all kinds are readily available and some have the potential to support entrepreneurs. But I do worry that as tech giants race ahead to push out their next AI model, there is insufficient attention on the actual utility of this technology to our small business owners and, frankly, to the American people.

The call is coming from inside the house. AI researchers themselves are warning of an existential threat to humanity.

Congress can’t wait. Mike Johnson needs to cancel recess so we can get to work immediately – hearings, investigations, and comprehensive regulation. https://t.co/9ovsX3V3SA
The threat from AI is serious. We need a president who will take it seriously. https://t.co/L3zXDLUFin
